screening_question: Can openly accessible full-text or supporting files add a row-traceable, compatible external human-plasma corona source to the frozen R3 rank endpoint?

candidates.citation: Walkey et al., Protein Corona Fingerprinting Predicts the Cellular Interaction of Gold and Silver Nanoparticles, ACS Nano 2014, DOI 10.1021/nn406018q
candidates.license_and_release_boundary: Supporting information is downloadable from ACS/figshare, but no explicit redistributable open-data license was located for the workbook; retain as source-dependent screening material, not a public release asset.
candidates.reason: The source has insufficient overlap with the frozen R3 feature population and fails the predeclared per-batch coverage threshold. It cannot support a valid rank endpoint without changing the target or missingness protocol after inspection.

candidates.citation: Trinh et al., Nanoparticle Biomolecular Corona-Based Enrichment of Plasma Glycoproteins for N-Glycan Profiling and Application in Biomarker Discovery, ACS Nano 2022, DOI 10.1021/acsnano.1c09564
candidates.laboratory_anchor: Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland and collaborating institutions
candidates.reason: The article is useful biological context, but the public supporting package does not contain the sample-by-protein abundance matrix required to reconstruct row-traceable within-batch protein ranks. The available workbook is glycan-level rather than the required protein-LFQ endpoint.

claim_boundary: These screens document reproducible exclusion decisions. They do not create new model evidence, independent validation, lockbox evidence, external scientific reproduction, or user adoption.
